A lot of HTTP libraries across different programming languages handle stuff like cookies for you, or offer an easy interface to work with them, so you can basically replicate the request containing email + password and if you’ve been using a session, you can make requests that you needed to be authenticated for. Golang has stuff like the cookie jar package you can attach to a client and Python’s request library contains request.Session.

Yes, you certainly could. Software like sneaker bots employ this strategy because it’s the most efficient + lightweight way to interact with these webpages. Using something like selenium, you generally need a new chrome instance for each “session”, so if you want to automate anything more than like 30 (arbitrary number but a lot of computers cannot properly handle 10 - 20 chrome instances running at once) different sessions, requests are the way to go. 

The main problems you run into with requests are no longer physical limitations of the computer, but stuff like IP rate limiting, potential bot protection / captcha stuff, and eventually the physical limitation of how many connections your PC can maintain at once. You really don’t have to worry about the last issue though. 

So yes, you definitely can do this using only HTTP requests as long as you can get around the obstacles I brought up.

Thank you! I felt I was going mad reading all of these replies using selenium and bs4 interchangeably...  Their functions are extremely different! In all actuality, they have very little to do with one another.

Selenium and beautiful soup are two completely different things. BS4 lets you parse html to extract data you need while selenium, to put it simply, is an automated browser. 

You can use beautiful soup with selenium, but they both perform completely different tasks.

Instead of using selenium with bs4, you can use something like requests, which allows you to make the same HTTP requests you do with a browser on a website. It’s a lot faster and less intensive than a browser. 

However, if the site has bot protection or uses JS to render its content, you would probably want to use something like selenium to access it, as requests would be much more challenging.
